root_hub_pointer_derivation_gate.purpose: Make root-hub pointer staleness mechanically detectable by deriving mandatory coverage sets from the candidate tree instead of relying on a hand-maintained gardening snapshot.

derivation_rules.normalization: Compare each entry_points[*].current_path after stripping one leading slash and any #fragment suffix.
derivation_rules.expectation: Every candidate-tree top-level specs/*.json file has at least one entry_points row whose normalized current_path base equals that repo-relative path. The list of required spec paths is never stored in this file.

derivation_rules.normalization: Strip one leading slash and any #fragment suffix; resolve against the repo root.
derivation_rules.expectation: Every non-retired current_path base resolves to an existing candidate-tree path. Until the legacy debt below is settled, the gate fails only on changes to the exact debt set.

derivation_rules.normalization: JSON Pointer fragments use RFC 6901. Dotted fragments in historical rows are accepted only when each segment resolves through object keys after the base JSON file parses.
derivation_rules.expectation: After current_path_base_reachability is clean, fragment resolution becomes an error gate instead of an advisory trace.

gate_expectations.expectation: Parse specs/root-hub-pointers.json as canonical JSON before evaluating any pointer rows.
Derive /specs/*.json from the candidate tree and reject any missing root-hub entry_points coverage. This replaces static counts such as specs_directory_audit_2026_05_20.top_level_specs_count.

Compute unresolved current_path base rows and require the set to exactly match known_current_path_debt_2026_06_30 until a cleanup slice removes the debt rows. Any new missing path or silently fixed debt row is a gate-visible diff.
Consumers must not use specs_directory_audit_2026_05_20 for current coverage claims; it is historical only and intentionally superseded by derived candidate-tree checks.
